newsitem.title: INDIA: Searchers find recorders in Saudi Airlines debris.
newsitem.headline: Searchers find recorders in Saudi Airlines debris.

text.p: The so-called "black boxes" from the Saudi Arabian Airlines plane involved in the world's worst mid-air collision, which killed some 350 people, have been found, a senior Indian official said on Wednesday.
"We have recovered both the flight data recorder and the cockpit voice recorder, V.K. Chandna, India's Director of Air Safety, told Reuters.
"They look damaged, but we expect the inside to be safe and secure," he said.

The "black boxes" from a Kazakh freighter, the other plane involved in the disaster, were recovered earlier in the day in the debris of the Ilyushin IL-76 some 10 km (six miles) from where the Saudi Boeing 747 plunged to earth on Tuesday.
Chandna said the recorders would be taken to New Delhi, where they would be analysed over the next few days to determine the cause of the as-yet unexplained collision.
